text:
maria (Design): Thinking about adding a persistent "skip to main" link at the top of the Console so keyboard users can jump straight to primary content. Quick mock attached in Figma. Thoughts?

sam (Frontend): Like this. Two concerns: 1) client-side route changes currently steal focus so the skip link might land on the wrong element after navigation, 2) need visual styles that don't flash for mouse users but are discoverable for keyboard. :eyes:

jordan (Product): We saw keyboard users struggle on the insights dashboard yesterday — filters open a flyout and focus gets stuck in the flyout until you refresh. Definitely want to avoid additional traps.

maria (Design): For visual states I was thinking of the classic offscreen -> visible on :focus pattern. For the focus-after-nav issue, propose we set a single focus target with tabindex="-1" id="main" and on route change call document.getElementById('main').focus();. That should preserve semantics and avoid outline jumps.

olivia (A11y): FYI VoiceOver on Safari also likes an ARIA announcement when major content changes, but we've got an annoying double-announcement right now. Likely coming from both our aria-live region + router status message. We should consolidate.

kevin (Eng): Quick implementation note: when focusing a non-focusable container we need tabindex="-1" and a small setTimeout(0) if the route is asynchronous so browser focus doesn't get swallowed. Example snippet: `const main = document.getElementById('main'); main && (main.tabIndex = -1, main.focus());`

maria (Design): Good call on debounce. Also want to make sure skiplink order doesn't collide with our global banner CTA which is first in DOM. Maybe render skip link as first element but visually hidden until focus.

axe-bot: Automated scan result: 3 issues found in /console/dashboard — 1) insufficient contrast on status chips (AA fail), 2) modal close buttons missing aria-labels, 3) keyboard focus not visible on compound control. See /ci/reports/1824999999/a11y.json

olivia (A11y): For the double announcement: check for role="status" + aria-live and any programmatic route-announcements. Remove role="status" where we already use polite live region, or switch one to aria-hidden until loaded.

sam (Frontend): I'll open a draft PR to add the skip link and the focus-preservation helper. Also will add a small utility: `focusOnLoad(el) { if (!el) return; el.tabIndex = -1; requestAnimationFrame(()=> el.focus()); }`

jordan (Product): Can we add a quick test case to our manual QA checklist—keyboard: tab to skip link, press Enter, verify focus lands on main header and screen reader announces new content just once.

maria (Design): Yep — adding to the checklist and will update the Figma to show visible focus outline color and the skip link text copy: "Skip to main content". Keep copy short.

kevin (Eng): Tagging PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4527 — includes skip link, focus helper, and fixes to modal return-focus. Still need to address contrast chips (separate PR).

olivia (A11y): Quick contrast suggestion: increase chip background darkness by 8% and use `color-contrast()` token where available. I'll run axe locally once PR lands.

maria (Design): Awesome — thanks everyone. If no objections I'll merge once CI passes and olivia signs off on axe results. :thumbsup:

sam (Frontend): Sounds good. I'll also add unit test to ensure focus is set on route change in Router.test.js

kevin (Eng): Will monitor staging for regressions. If we see focus jumps we can add a page-level focus guard.

olivia (A11y): Thanks — ping me in PR comments for quick verification.

maria (Design): Closing loop — created ticket ENG-1283 to follow up on chip contrast and announcements consolidation.

jordan (Product): Nice, thanks all.
